title: Internal edge router Terraform module — NLB-to-ALB routing, TLS modes, and healthcheck policies
creator: Arjun Patel
description:
Goal: Build a reusable Terraform module that implements an internal edge router for Private (VPC) deployments supporting: (1) NLB passthrough, (2) ALB TLS termination with host/path routing, and (3) configurable health checks and connection stickiness. This module will be the recommended ingress pattern for on-prem and VPC private deployments where customers need predictable routing, client IP preservation, and simple certificate rotation policies.

Scope:
- Create a single module that can create either or both load balancers and wire Target Groups/Listeners according to variables (e.g., enable_nlb, enable_alb, tls_mode = ["alb","nlb","passthrough"]).
- Support internal scheme for both ALB and NLB and create appropriate subnet mappings for private subnets.
- Pluggable certificate support: ACM cert ARN input (for ALB) and option to attach certificates at NLB (TLS listener) for TCP TLS termination where desired.
- Health checks: explicit defaults (HTTP /healthz, interval 10s, timeout 5s, healthy 3, unhealthy 2) with ability to override per target-group. For NLB/TCP backends, fallback to TCP health checks on application port.
- Stickiness and session controls: optional ALB cookie stickiness and NLB source/destination preservation toggles.
- Upgrade & migration plan: helpers to create new target groups and do blue-green switch using weight-based routing on ALB where available; instructions for cutover with minimal connection disruption for NLB.
- Observability: output ARNs, DNS names, target group IDs, listener ARNs and create CloudWatch metric filters for healthy/unhealthy host counts.

Design decisions / trade-offs:
- ALB vs NLB: ALB recommended when we need host/path routing and HTTP-level health checks; NLB recommended when low latency, TCP passthrough, or client IP preservation is required. Module supports both to cover hybrid customer needs.
- TLS termination options: terminating TLS on ALB simplifies certificate rotation via ACM; terminating on NLB may be required for upstream TLS or when customer requires passthrough. Allow both modes but warn in docs about cross-zone connection behavior and source IP preservation differences.
- Health checks: prefer HTTP/HTTPS for application-aware checks, fallback to TCP for legacy backends. Default path is /healthz to standardize across services; allow explicit override in target-group map.
- Security: all load balancers are created with internal scheme by default and require explicit boolean to expose externally. Restrict security groups to MSC (managed service connectivity) CIDR lists and expose variables for additional allowed CIDRs.

Deliverables:
- Terraform module published under infra-modules/load-balancer-edge with examples for: simple ALB termination, NLB passthrough, mixed (NLB in front of ALB for TLS passthrough then termination), and blue-green target-group swap.
- Unit tests (tflint, terraform validate, fmt) and CI plan step that runs against a mock account (or staging account) to terraform plan and basic apply in a disposable env.
- Documentation page with migration checklist from legacy ingress stacks and runbook for certificate rotation and emergency rollback.

Risks / open questions:
- Cross-account or shared VPC patterns: module should accept explicit subnet IDs and SGs but we need a follow-up to validate for AWS Transit and shared VPC setups.
- IPv6 support not in initial PR; to be scoped separately.
- Health-check matcher behavior for HTTP 3xx redirects: decide whether 3xx should count as healthy (default will accept 200-399).
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module lives at infra-modules/load-balancer-edge with README and examples
Module can create ALB-only, NLB-only, and NLB+ALB hybrid topologies via variables
Default health check policy applied and overridable per target group
TLS mode variable supports 'alb', 'nlb', and 'passthrough' with documented caveats
Module outputs stable identifiers (dns_name, alb_listener_arn, nlb_dns, target_group_ids) and publishes to module registry
Integration smoke test in staging successfully registers targets and reports healthy hosts
Security review completed and infra-Sec approves default SGs and policy

Implement conditional creation logic and lifecycle rules for blue-green swap
Add health-check override map and sensible defaults
Add acceptance CI job (plan/apply in isolated staging account) and tflint checks
Prepare docs and migration runbook; include certificate rotation steps and rollback steps
Open PR and iterate on review feedback from PM, SEC, and SRE

2025-02-24 - Security (Lena Cho): Flagged need for explicit SG examples and hard deny for 0.0.0.0/0 on internal ALB. Requested documentation for least-privileged IAM for module's CI pipeline.

2025-02-28 - SRE (Miguel Alvarez): Suggested adding CloudWatch alarms for UnhealthyHostCount > 0 for more than 2 intervals and a dashboard widget for target group health. Also recommended graceful timeout values for longer boot times on some customers' containers.
